answers: Tomato is best irrigated lightly and frequently, especially via drip irrigation, avoiding both waterlogging and drought stress, particularly during flowering and fruit set.
Most crops perform best in a soil pH range of about 6.0 to 7.5 (slightly acidic to neutral); get a soil test done for your specific field before amending pH.
Groundnut is typically sown at the start of the Kharif season (June-July) or Rabi season (post-monsoon), depending on regional rainfall patterns.
Nitrogen deficiency commonly shows as uniform yellowing (chlorosis) starting from older, lower leaves, along with stunted and slow overall growth.
Yellowing of rice leaves can result from nitrogen deficiency, zinc deficiency, bacterial leaf blight, or waterlogging/drainage stress; the growth stage and pattern of yellowing help narrow the cause.
Yellow sticky traps, neem-based sprays, avoiding excess nitrogen, and encouraging natural predators such as ladybird beetles are common organic approaches to manage whitefly.
Crop rotation is growing different crop types in sequence on the same land across seasons; it helps break pest/disease cycles, balances soil nutrient use, and improves long-term soil health.
Avoid applying fertilizer immediately before heavy rain since it can wash away nutrients; dry, low-wind conditions are generally best for foliar sprays.
Rice is generally ready for harvest when about 80-85% of the grains have turned golden yellow and the moisture content of the grain has dropped appropriately.
IPM combines biological, cultural, mechanical and (as a last resort) chemical methods to manage pests sustainably while minimizing environmental and health risks.

Rice (நெல்) is a cereal crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 90-150 days. Staple cereal grown widely in Tamil Nadu deltas; needs standing water for most growth stages. It prefers clayey loam, water-retentive soil and a temperature range of 20-35°C.

Wheat (கோதுமை) is a cereal crop typically grown in the Rabi season, maturing in about 110-130 days. Major cereal in North India; sensitive to waterlogging and needs a cool growing period. It prefers well-drained loam soil and a temperature range of 10-25°C.

Maize (சோளம்) is a cereal crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 90-110 days. Versatile cereal used for food, fodder and industry; moderate water requirement. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 18-27°C.

Cotton (பருத்தி) is a fibre crop typically grown in the Kharif season, maturing in about 150-180 days. Fibre crop needing a long frost-free season and moderate, well-spaced irrigation. It prefers black cotton soil (regur) soil and a temperature range of 21-30°C.

Sugarcane (கரும்பு) is a cash crop crop typically grown in the Year-round (12 month crop) season, maturing in about 300-365 days. Long-duration cash crop with high water demand, propagated via stem cuttings. It prefers deep, well-drained loam soil and a temperature range of 21-27°C.

Groundnut (நிலக்கடலை) is a oilseed/legume crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 100-130 days. Legume oilseed that fixes atmospheric nitrogen and needs calcium during pegging. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 20-30°C.

Tomato (தக்காளி) is a vegetable crop typically grown in the Year-round (season dependent) season, maturing in about 60-90 days. Widely grown vegetable, sensitive to blossom-end rot and several fungal/bacterial diseases. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 20-27°C.

Banana (வாழை) is a fruit crop typically grown in the Year-round season, maturing in about 10-13 months. High water and nutrient demanding fruit crop, propagated using suckers/tissue-culture plants. It prefers deep, rich, well-drained loam soil and a temperature range of 15-35°C.

Chilli (மிளகாய்) is a vegetable/spice crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 120-180 days. Spice crop sensitive to thrips, mites and viral leaf curl disease. It prefers well-drained sandy loam soil and a temperature range of 20-30°C.

Blackgram (உளுந்து) is a pulse/legume crop typically grown in the Kharif/Rabi season, maturing in about 70-90 days. Short-duration pulse commonly grown as a rice-fallow crop; improves soil nitrogen. It prefers well-drained loam to clay loam soil and a temperature range of 25-35°C.

Bacterial Leaf Blight (பாக்டீரியா இலை கருகல் நோய்) affects Rice and is caused by Xanthomonas oryzae. Symptoms include: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins turning yellow-white and drying from tip inward.
Management of Bacterial Leaf Blight: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, ensure field sanitation and balanced water management; consult an expert for approved bactericides.

Rice Blast (நெல் வெடிப்பு நோய்) affects Rice and is caused by Magnaporthe oryzae (fungus). Symptoms include: Diamond/spindle shaped grey-centered lesions with brown margins on leaves, neck rot at panicle base.
Management of Rice Blast: Use resistant varieties, avoid dense nursery, balanced nitrogen; fungicidal seed treatment as advised by an agricultural officer.

Late Blight (பிற்பாதி கருகல் நோய்) affects Tomato and is caused by Phytophthora infestans (oomycete). Symptoms include: Dark water-soaked patches on leaves and stems with white fungal growth under humid conditions, fruit rot.
Management of Late Blight: Improve field drainage and air circulation, remove infected debris, use certified disease-free seedlings; fungicide only under expert guidance.

Fusarium Wilt (பியூசேரியம் வாட்டநோய்) affects Cotton, Tomato, Banana and is caused by Fusarium oxysporum (fungus). Symptoms include: Yellowing and wilting of lower leaves progressing upward, vascular browning inside stem.
Management of Fusarium Wilt: Practice crop rotation, use resistant/tolerant varieties, avoid waterlogging, solarize nursery soil before sowing.

Powdery Mildew (பொடி பூஞ்சை நோய்) affects Groundnut, Chilli, many crops and is caused by Erysiphe / Oidium spp. (fungus). Symptoms include: White powdery fungal growth on upper leaf surface, leaf curling and premature drying.
Management of Powdery Mildew: Ensure good airflow between plants, avoid excess nitrogen, remove heavily infected leaves; sulfur-based fungicide only per label/expert advice.
Panama Wilt (பனாமா வாட்டநோய்) affects Banana and is caused by Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense. Symptoms include: Yellowing of older leaves, splitting of pseudostem base, plant collapse.
Management of Panama Wilt: Use tissue-culture disease-free planting material, avoid waterlogged soil, do not replant bananas in infected fields for several years.

Leaf Curl Virus (இலை சுருள் வைரஸ் நோய்) affects Chilli, Tomato and is caused by Begomovirus (whitefly transmitted). Symptoms include: Upward/downward curling of leaves, stunted growth, reduced fruiting.
Management of Leaf Curl Virus: Control whitefly vector with sticky traps and recommended practices, remove infected plants early, use virus-tolerant varieties.

Blackgram Yellow Mosaic (மஞ்சள் தேமல் நோய்) affects Blackgram, Greengram and is caused by Mungbean yellow mosaic virus (whitefly transmitted). Symptoms include: Irregular yellow mosaic patches on leaves, stunted pods.
Management of Blackgram Yellow Mosaic: Sow tolerant varieties, manage whitefly populations, remove volunteer/alternate host plants near field borders.

Urea (யூரியா) supplies Nitrogen (N) - 46% and is suitable for Rice, Maize, Wheat, most cereals. Recommended application: Vegetative growth stage, split doses. Fast-acting nitrogen source promoting leafy growth; apply in split doses to reduce leaching loss.

DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate) (டிஏபி உரம்) supplies Nitrogen (18%) + Phosphorus (46%) and is suitable for Most crops at sowing/transplanting. Recommended application: Basal application at sowing/transplanting. Provides early-stage phosphorus for root development, usually applied as a basal dose.

MOP (Muriate of Potash) (மியூரியேட் ஆஃப் பொட்டாஷ்) supplies Potassium (K) - 60% and is suitable for Fruiting/tuber crops, sugarcane, banana. Recommended application: Flowering / fruit development stage. Improves fruit quality, disease resistance and drought tolerance; important during reproductive stages.

Farmyard Manure (FYM) (தொழு உரம்) supplies Organic matter, N-P-K + micronutrients and is suitable for All crops. Recommended application: Basal application before sowing/planting. Improves soil structure, water-holding capacity and microbial activity over the long term.

Vermicompost (மண்புழு உரம்) supplies Organic matter, balanced N-P-K + micronutrients and is suitable for All crops, especially vegetables. Recommended application: Basal + top dressing. Slow-release organic fertilizer that improves soil health; widely used in organic farming.

Single Super Phosphate (SSP) (சிங்கிள் சூப்பர் பாஸ்பேட்) supplies Phosphorus (16%) + Calcium + Sulphur and is suitable for Oilseeds, pulses, general crops. Recommended application: Basal application at sowing. Economical phosphorus source that also supplies sulphur, useful for oilseed and pulse crops.

Zinc Sulphate (துத்தநாக சல்பேட்) supplies Micronutrient - Zinc and is suitable for Rice, Citrus, most crops on zinc-deficient soil. Recommended application: Soil application or foliar spray. Corrects zinc deficiency symptoms such as leaf bronzing/khaira disease in rice; test soil before applying.

NPK Complex (19:19:19) (என்பிகே கூட்டு உரம்) supplies Balanced Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium and is suitable for Vegetables, fruit crops, general use. Recommended application: Vegetative and flowering stage, foliar or soil. Water-soluble balanced fertilizer suited for fertigation and foliar feeding programs.

For Rice, the recommended method is Flood/Continuous submergence or AWD (Alternate Wetting & Drying). 2-5 cm standing water during vegetative stage; AWD saves water without yield loss Maintaining shallow standing water during flowering is critical; avoid stress at panicle initiation.

For Wheat, the recommended method is Furrow / Sprinkler. 4-6 irrigations at critical growth stages (CRI, tillering, flowering, grain filling) Crown root initiation (CRI) stage irrigation is the most critical for yield.

For Cotton, the recommended method is Drip / Furrow. Irrigate at 50-60% depletion of available soil moisture Avoid water stress during flowering and boll development; drip irrigation improves water-use efficiency.

For Sugarcane, the recommended method is Furrow / Drip. Frequent irrigation every 7-10 days depending on soil and season High water requirement crop; drip irrigation with fertigation significantly improves efficiency.

For Tomato, the recommended method is Drip irrigation recommended. Light, frequent irrigation; avoid water stress during flowering/fruit set Irregular watering increases blossom-end rot and fruit cracking.
For Groundnut, the recommended method is Sprinkler / Furrow. Critical stages: pegging and pod development Avoid waterlogging; groundnut is sensitive to excess soil moisture at sowing.

Brown Planthopper (பழுப்பு தத்துப்பூச்சி) is a sap-sucking insect affecting Rice. Damage symptoms: Hopper burn: yellowing and drying of plants in circular patches. Management: Avoid excess nitrogen, use resistant varieties, encourage natural predators like spiders and mirid bugs.

Stem Borer (தண்டு துளைப்பான்) is a larval boring insect affecting Rice, Maize, Sugarcane. Damage symptoms: Dead heart in vegetative stage, white ear head at reproductive stage. Management: Use pheromone traps, remove and destroy affected tillers, encourage egg-parasitoid release (Trichogramma).

Whitefly (வெள்ளை ஈ) is a sap-sucking insect & virus vector affecting Cotton, Chilli, Tomato. Damage symptoms: Yellowing, sooty mould from honeydew, transmits leaf curl viruses. Management: Use yellow sticky traps, avoid excess nitrogen, encourage natural predators; rotate non-host crops.

Fall Armyworm (இலை உண்ணும் புழு) is a leaf/whorl feeding caterpillar affecting Maize. Damage symptoms: Window-pane feeding damage on young leaves, ragged holes on whorl leaves. Management: Scout fields regularly, hand-pick egg masses, encourage natural enemies, use pheromone traps for monitoring.

Pod Borer (காய் துளைப்பான்) is a larval boring insect affecting Groundnut, Blackgram, Pulses. Damage symptoms: Circular holes bored into pods/flowers, larval frass visible. Management: Deploy pheromone traps, encourage bird perches, avoid continuous monoculture.

Thrips (நுண்பூச்சி) is a rasping-sucking insect affecting Chilli, Onion, Groundnut. Damage symptoms: Silvery streaks on leaves, curling and crinkling of young leaves. Management: Use blue sticky traps, avoid moisture stress, encourage predatory mites and bugs.

Alluvial Soil (வண்டல் மண்) is characterized by: Fertile, well-drained, rich in potash, deposited by rivers. It suits crops such as Rice, Wheat, Sugarcane, Maize. Most fertile Indian soil type found in river plains and deltas; good for a wide crop range.

Black Cotton Soil (Regur) (கருப்பு பருத்தி மண்) is characterized by: High clay content, high water-retention, cracks when dry. It suits crops such as Cotton, Groundnut, Sugarcane, Sorghum. Rich in lime, iron, magnesium; retains moisture well but drains slowly, needs careful water management.

Red Soil (செம்மண்) is characterized by: Low nitrogen and organic matter, well-drained, red due to iron oxide. It suits crops such as Groundnut, Millets, Pulses, Tobacco. Common in Tamil Nadu uplands; responds well to organic manure and balanced fertilization.

Laterite Soil (லேட்டரைட் மண்) is characterized by: Acidic, low fertility, high iron/aluminium content. It suits crops such as Cashew, Tea, Coffee, Rubber. Found in high rainfall regions; needs liming and organic matter to improve fertility.

Sandy Loam (மணல் கலந்த களிமண்) is characterized by: Good drainage, moderate water-holding capacity, easy to till. It suits crops such as Groundnut, Vegetables, Chilli. Warms quickly in spring and is easy to work, but may need more frequent irrigation.

Clayey Soil (களிமண்) is characterized by: High water-retention, poor drainage, nutrient-rich. It suits crops such as Rice, Sugarcane. Suitable for standing-water crops like rice; needs good drainage management for other crops.
